conversation.message: What exactly are photovoltaic panels?

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Photovoltaic panels, also known as solar panels, are devices that convert light directly into electricity at the atomic level. They are made of semiconductor materials, most commonly silicon.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: How do these panels convert light into electricity?

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: When photons from sunlight strike the semiconductor material, they knock electrons loose, creating an electric current. This process is called the photovoltaic effect.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: There are indeed different types, primarily monocrystalline, polycrystalline, and thin-film, each with unique characteristics and applications.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Monocrystalline panels are known for high efficiency and sleek appearance, while polycrystalline panels are more cost-effective. Thin-film panels offer flexibility and can be integrated into various surfaces.
